  • Algonquin↗Historical homeland and continuing cultural connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland and continuing cultural connection

    The Canadian Heritage Rivers System's Ottawa River, Ontario page identifies the Ontario heritage-river segment as the cultural heartland of the Algonquin people. Its plaque text describes the Ottawa River as flowing through Algonquin Traditional Territory and names Kitchisippi. Used for an Ontario regional connection only, not a claim over the entire province or an adjudication of modern land claims. The actual page was read, including Designation and Plaque Text; community-site and Natural Resources Canada requests failed and were not substituted as inspected evidence.

    Historical territory described on the current heritage-river page; inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

  • Munsee↗Present community government location; one Munsee access point
    Connection & source
    Present community government location; one Munsee access point

    Munsee-Delaware Nation identifies itself as a Lunaape band government on the northern shore of the Thames River, southwest of London, Ontario. This provides a present Ontario route for the broader Munsee directory entry through one specific Lenape-related community. Inspection: Read About page's opening paragraph and Lenni Lenape history paragraphs; language section also inspected but not used for classification. Limits: The Munsee directory access point encompasses more than this one government. Do not merge Munsee-Delaware Nation with Stockbridge-Munsee Community, Eelūnaapèewii Lahkèewiit, or other Lenape governments. No population, land-area, subgroup taxonomy, or language-family assertion is adopted from this page.

    Contemporary community self-description, inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Neutral Nation↗Historical confederation/community connection
    Connection & source
    Historical confederation/community connection

    The museum identifies historical Neutral communities around Lincoln and the northern shores of Lakes Ontario and Erie; its public interpretation site is in Jordan, Ontario. It treats Neutral Nation, Attawandaron and Hatiwendaronk as historical naming forms while explicitly noting uncertainty about the people's own name. Inspection: Read the historical introduction, The Neutral Nation paragraphs, and Location section. The Town of Lincoln's 2026 research-collection announcement was also inspected through its full indexed text and explicitly confirms southern Ontario/Niagara. Limits: Historical groups are not equated with a single contemporary government; dispersal does not establish disappearance of descendants. No exact archaeological or burial location is reproduced. The modern park's Mohawk spelling, contemporary art, and ceremonies are not generalized as historical Neutral language or practices. Direct fetch of the municipal announcement failed; the main museum interpretation page was accessible and read directly.

    Historical early-seventeenth-century communities; current museum interpretation inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗ · Supporting source 1 ↗
